items.stem: Why are loops so useful in generative art?

options.text: They let you repeat and vary many shapes with a small amount of code
options.rationale: Correct: loops efficiently create repeated, varied visual elements.
Loops repeat drawing code; they do not change brightness.

options.text: They stop the program from drawing
options.rationale: Loops are used to draw repeatedly, not to stop drawing.

options.text: They can only draw a single shape once
options.rationale: Loops are specifically for repeating many shapes.

items.explanation: Correct: loops efficiently create repeated, varied visual elements.

items.stem: Which TWO techniques add variation so each run of a generative piece looks different? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Using randomness for positions or colours
options.rationale: Correct: randomness changes the output each run.

options.text: Using noise to vary values smoothly
Drawing exactly the same fixed picture every time
options.rationale: A fixed picture produces no variation.
Turning off the screen does not create artistic variation.

items.explanation: Correct: randomness changes the output each run.

items.stem: You want a pattern to feel random but still look balanced, not messy. What should you do?

options.text: Use randomness within sensible limits (constrain the range of values)
options.rationale: Correct: controlled/constrained randomness keeps variety while staying balanced.

options.text: Remove all randomness so it is identical each time
Let every value be fully random with no limits
Use no loops or variables at all
options.rationale: Loops and variables help structure the composition.

items.explanation: Correct: controlled/constrained randomness keeps variety while staying balanced.
